challenge.method: Compare p.19 with p.20, the CHM profile, and Flake, Moorby, Golson, Salz and Davidmann (2020), §4.1, DOI 10.1145/3386337. Test whether the early tool emphasis is the same proposition as the original goals of designing the language, and whether Gateway was the contemporaneous business name.
challenge.results: The attributed interview statement is explicit. The 2020 coauthored history treats synthesis and verification as equal primary language-design motives and fault simulation among secondary tools. It also describes the startup's original name as Automated Integrated Design Systems, later renamed Gateway. These qualify the framing without disputing what Moorby recalled.

limitations: This is testimony about the period, not a ranking of independently established corporate or design priorities. Gateway is the later name used for the same startup.
The publisher DOI route returned 403. The coauthored article was inspected through author Arturo Salz's posted copy as a challenge, and it is not treated as independent corroboration of Moorby.
